subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a default-off session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39127 lands, or should core expose activity and diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards to consume?
rationale: The request adds new feature, config, delivery, privacy, UI/operator, and optional model-call behavior rather than repairing an existing contract, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
options.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical `sessions.activity` contract is settled.

options.title: Route alerting to plugins or dashboards
options.body: Core would expose activity and diagnostics while plugin, ClawHub, or external monitoring surfaces own alert delivery and summaries.

options.title: Fold into broader operator visibility
options.body: Use this as context for silence, delivery, and session-health work but require a narrower canonical implementation issue before coding.

recommendation.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical `sessions.activity` contract is settled.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned to the prerequisite public session activity API and has adjacent sessions-list history.
